av_event.what: A young girl in pyjamas walks across the room behind the sofa in the background, picks up the pink unicorn cushion and carries it out of shot to the right.

text:
B: Alright. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah.
B: Sound's a bit... no, it's fine, you're there. I'm Darren.
A: Kayleigh.
B: Nice one. Erm, I don't really know what we're meant to talk about. Just anything, I suppose.
A: Dunno really.
B: Right. Erm. You look like you've come off a shift. Sorry, that sounds rude. It's the lanyard. My partner's got one just like it.
A: Care home. I'm a carer.
B: No way, so's Gemma. My partner. Residential home, older people.
A: Funny, the girl I just had was a Gemma. Student nurse though. Where's yours work?
B: Just near us, Sutton-in-Ashfield. Notts. She's been doing it years. Her back's knackered from the lifting, honestly. They're meant to use the hoist with two of them, but there's never two free, so she just does it.
A: Yeah, that's every home. I'm not being funny but they want two on a hoist and then put four of you on for thirty residents. It's a joke. And the seniors won't help, they're sat in the office.
B: That's what she says, word for word nearly.
A: What do you do then?
B: Warehouse. Picking and loading at a distribution centre off the M1. Fifty-odd hours a week with the overtime. They time your breaks to the minute. Had a team leader stood over me with a scanner last week, mardy as anything, 'cause my pick rate dipped for an hour. I said, mate, I've been here since six.
A: They're all the same, managers. They don't do the actual job.
B: Exactly that. Do you know what I mean, if he got on the floor for a day he'd soon change his tune.
A: Ours wouldn't last a shift.
B: Is it twelve hours you do?
A: Yeah, mostly. Forty a week. I want to stop doing them, to be fair, but you need the money.
B: Yeah. That's it, isn't it. Petrol, bills, everything.
A: My car needs an MOT and I'm skint till payday. And school's asking for money for a trip again.
B: You got kids?
A: Daughter. She's ten.
B: Nice. We haven't. Just the dog, Mabel. Staffie cross, she's about twelve now, snores like a lorry.
A: Lacey wants a dog. Not happening.
B: Fair. Erm, your picture had that Live Laugh Love thing in it. Sorry, that's a weird thing to say. I just notice stuff in pictures. I draw a bit, you know. Buildings mostly.
A: That was off my mum. I wouldn't have bought it.
B: Ha, no. Mine's a drawing of a pit headstock, behind me there. Bit sad, probably.
A: No, that's alright, that. You did that?
B: Yeah, years ago. Did a year of art at college then packed it in.
A: I did a year of hair and beauty and packed that in. I do nails now, on the side, like.
B: Yeah? Gemma'd love that, she's always—
